newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mystery writer wrote about his death - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mystery writer wrote about his death - report.

text.p: Mystery writer Eugene Izzi, whose body was found hanging from his office window last month, wrote about a heroic escape from a similar predicament in an unpublished manuscript, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

Citing sources in the police department, the Chicago Tribune said computer discs in the 43-year-old writer's pockets held an 800-page manuscript containing tantalizing details that matched the scene of his death.

His body was found on Dec. 7 hanging from a rope outside the window of his high-rise downtown office. He was wearing a bullet-proof vest and had a can of chemical Mace in his pockets. There was a loaded revolver on the floor of his office.
His neck was not broken and the medical examiner has yet to determine the exact cause of death.

Several friends of the moderately successful writer do not believe he committed suicide and say he told them he had been threatened by a right-wing militia group he was investigating for his next novel. Others said Izzi had always been paranoid.

The Tribune said the manuscript contained a scene where the hero, a mystery writer, is hung out his office window by a militia member but escapes by hauling himself back in and kills his attacker with the gun.

The Tribune's sources theorised that Izzi, a stickler for realism in his well-researched mysteries, may have tried to lower himself out of his office window in an experiment that went wrong. Or it may be that the writer, who was undergoing treatment for depression, committed suicide and left a mystery behind.
